page: Microsoft Azure GS5-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, offering a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 56.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 918 GB, and there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between compute speed and memory capacity. Single-core CPU performance is poor, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scoring in the bottom 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5342.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 9973.73. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 617.21 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 63.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks show mixed results, with average gzip compression but weak bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption scores.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance trades raw CPU processing speed for massive memory capacity and local storage. It is designed for workloads requiring large memory footprints rather than intensive single-threaded compute power. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and memory-intensive database operations, as reflected by its average Redis SET performance of 11.02 million operations per second and average database operations score.
